extracted.intended_audience: news-organization managers, legal counsel, and historians researching press practices
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational policies and standards governing how a news agency (The Associated Press) and its employees must gather, verify, handle, and distribute news, and prohibitions on using competitors' material. The page is a set of affidavits responding to allegations about those practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on co-location with rival operators
rubrics_metrics.description: The uniform practice of The Associated Press is not to permit its correspondents or operators receiving or sending its news to perform these functions in the same room with the correspondent or telegraph operator of any other news-agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule exists to prevent rival operators from obtaining news by overhearing or reading instruments. The Syracuse courthouse situation was described as peculiar and unusual (exceptional circumstance), but the rule is the standard practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule forbidding rivals from occupying member newspaper offices/buildings
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainant established a rule some years ago prohibiting its members from permitting the telegraph operators or representatives of any other news agencies to send or receive news or occupy any room or office in the building where such newspaper was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopted to prevent competing agencies from obtaining the complainant's news by proximity; this rule has been rigidly enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining news by inducing breach of contract or confidential relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any charge that operators were expected or permitted to obtain such information or rumor by inducing any breach of a contract or confidential relation or to use information which they knew to have been communicated under circumstances of such a breach, is wholly untrue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any operator discovered doing so would be discharged. Instances, if they occurred, were unauthorized and without management knowledge or approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting rumors to controlling bureau (but not using them as finished stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Associated Press operators, when learning in any legitimate way of a rumor of an event or happening anywhere, should send to their controlling bureau points the fact of the rumor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only use of rumors is for the information of our correspondents in the district where the event is reported to have happened. Rumors are not to be sent out as authoritative stories without independent verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent investigation requirement for all dispatched stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Any despatches The Associated Press sends out are based upon its own independent investigation and the product of its own enterprise and expense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a rumor or report is received, AP investigates through its own sources; any story sent to members must be based solely upon news obtained by AP correspondents from original sources, and if no such information can be obtained, no story is sent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on rewriting or republishing opposition-service stories
rubrics_metrics.description: It is the definite, invariable and well understood policy of The Associated Press to base no stories upon tips received from opposition services and that at no time should any story appearing in opposition news services be rewritten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors and employees are specifically instructed never to rewrite stories originating in opposition services; reading rival newspapers is routine, but rewriting those items for AP distribution is forbidden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial handling of tips: verify from original sources before distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: If the news editor at the central office considers information (a tip) of real value, he will send a message to the AP correspondent in the district where the event was reported; the correspondent would independently investigate the story from original sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports sent to members will be based solely upon the strength of such independent investigation. If such original-source information cannot be obtained, the invariable practice is to send out no story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator duty under General Order No. 353 to protect AP coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Operators who copy the report in newspaper offices at non-bureau points should be alert to see that The Associated Press is protected promptly when big news events occur in their cities; they should immediately call to the attention of editors the necessity of a bulletin, and if a bulletin is not quickly offered, should themselves send a message of information to their controlling bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureau points will make note of such assistance on the operator's service record; the order refers to local news where non-bureau operators can help secure prompt AP coverage and is not intended to encourage inducing breaches of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: No use of rival news dispatches before or after publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Such correspondents and representatives have not been authorized to use the news despatches, either in whole or in part, before or after publication, of any rival or competing news-gathering association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: So far as deponents know, The Associated Press has not done so; any action based on rival dispatches rather than AP's independent investigation would contravene policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement and disciplinary consequences for violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Any employe discovered violating rules (e.g., using rival service material, inducing breaches, rewriting opposition stories) would be dismissed from the service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management states that unauthorized instances would be rare, wholly unauthorized, and without management approval; the policy is communicated to employees and violations are grounds for discharge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Routine filing practice for original copy
rubrics_metrics.description: The original 'copy' of any stories transmitted over the wires of the Association is placed in the general record filing room in filing cabinets under its respective dates for office reference; the routine has never included filing with the Superintendent as alleged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural detail was offered to counter an allegation about supervisory knowledge/control and indicates how records are maintained and what supervisors routinely see.
